newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen gaining after tame CPI.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen gaining after tame CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to gain at the market open on Wednesday, buoyed by the release of the June consumer price index, which showed almost no sign of inflation, and by a strong technology sector.

The Labor Department reported the CPI rose 0.1 percent in June, compared with a forecast gain of 0.2 percent and a 0.1 percent rise in May. Excluding food and energy prices, the core CPI rose 0.1 percent.
"The CPI was a pleasant surprise," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "The overall trend is up and the focus is on earnings expansion."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 5.10 points at 936.80 following the release of the data, and bonds firmed 10/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
"Stocks are likely to open higher," Ackerman said.
Technology stocks should lead the broader equities market higher, after solid results from giant chipmaker Intel Corp, analysts said.
But below-forecast results from Eastman Kodak Co could hamper the Dow's rise, they said.
Kodak posted second quarter earnings of $1.12 per share, falling short of Wall Street analysts' forecasts.
